back: An agreement allowing a franchisee to use a franchisor's brand, products and methods in return for fees and royalties.
The business that owns the brand and sells franchises.
The person or business that buys a franchise and runs an outlet under the brand.
A regular payment from franchisee to franchisor, often a percentage of sales.
Independent businesses sharing the capital, risks, control and profits of a project.
A business with mainly social or environmental aims that reinvests most of its surplus in them.
Gains a known brand, training and advertising; loses part of profit and freedom.
Expands quickly with others' capital and earns royalties; risks brand damage and loses direct control.
In a joint venture firms stay separate and cooperate on one project; in a merger they become one business.
